subject: High p95/p99 for Hosted API — QuickCommerce production spike
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@quickcommerce.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency & 502s in prod — QuickCommerce

Alex / Marissa,

We're seeing a major degradation in our Checkout flow starting ~15:45 PDT — p95 and p99 latencies for calls to /v1/generate jumped to ~3.2s / 7.8s respectively and a lot of our checkout calls are returning 502/504 or timing out on the client side. Our incident page: https://status.quickcommerce.com/incident/5543 shows customer impact (some merchants offline).

Sample request IDs from our logs: rq_7f9a3b, rq_7f9a6c, rq_7f9aaf. We also see a surge in retries from the same customer IP ranges and repeated identical payloads. Can you confirm if there was a platform-side change or a regional issue? We need an RCA and immediate mitigation — our ops team is advising to throttle calls from our side but we'd prefer to understand the root cause first.

I've attached a small CSV of our error-rate timeline and a few sample traces (attachment stub: quickcommerce_errors_20270428.csv).

Thanks — this is high priority for us.

Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, QuickCommerce
elaine.park@quickcommerce.com

Subject: Re: Severe latency & 502s in prod — QuickCommerce

Elaine —

Thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs. We're treating this as an incident and I’ve looped in our SRE/tech leads. Initial ask from our side: if you can temporarily increase your per-request timeout (client-side) to 30s and reduce retries (disable aggressive immediate retries) while we investigate, it will reduce amplification and help collectors get a stable picture.

I'll share an internal update in 30–60 minutes with what we see from the ingress, but if you want immediate mitigation and your team can change the SDK config quickly that would help avoid further retries.

We have access to the request IDs you provided and will correlate traces. I’ll update shortly.

— Alex Martinez

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe latency & 502s in prod — QuickCommerce

Folks — forwarding QuickCommerce's note below. Quick summary: p95/p99 spike visible in customer dashboard, and they report a lot of client retries. Please treat this as customer-facing incident (QC on a paid Dedicated seat).

Initial hypotheses:
- Platform transient 5xxs and a short CPU saturation window triggered client retries (amplification).
- Alternatively (and more likely based on the sample traces), the QuickCommerce SDK is configured with short timeouts and non-exponential retry backoff which generates a retry storm for a subset of requests.

Actions: Sergio — can you pull ingress QPS, 5xx rate, and trace spans for the request IDs they sent (rq_7f9a3b etc.) and check if retries originate from the same client SDK version / IPs? Tessa — prep a throttling policy we can enable per-customer (short-term) that won't break them. Marissa — I may need a customer call later; please prepare account context and the contract SLA notes.

I'll collect what Sergio finds and coordinate the external update.

Thanks,
Alex
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe latency & 502s in prod — QuickCommerce

Quick notes from the tracing/logs (initial):

- Ingress spike at 15:44–15:52 PDT: sustained 12x baseline QPS for QC's API key, coincident with p95/p99 spikes and an increase in 502/504s.
- Many requests show identical payloads + repeated request IDs across retries — pattern matches aggressive client retries.
- SDK fingerprinting shows rwd-sdk-js@0.9.1 in ~82% of requests from QC. That version has a backoff bug we flagged internally (backoff not increasing correctly when upstream latency grows).
- Example trace (shortened):
  On 2027-04-28T15:46:12Z rq_7f9a3b: initial call -> upstream slow (2000ms) -> client retries immediately (no jitter, 3 retries in 10s) -> backend queueing -> additional 5xxs.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Advise QC to increase client socket/request timeout to 30s and switch to exponential backoff with jitter (cap 4 retries). I'll paste a config snippet below and attach sdk-config-snippet.txt.
2) On our side, enable per-customer token-based request throttling for QC for the next 24 hours to break the amplification loop (low-risk, soft-429s then throttle). Tessa, can you stand this up?
3) Patch the JS SDK (release 0.9.2) to fix backoff behavior; shipping ETA 48 hours.

I'll keep digging into server-side traces for any code-path regressions, but current evidence strongly supports client retry amplification as the primary driver of the p95/p99 regression.

---
Suggested client config (rwd-sdk-js):
  timeoutMs: 30000
  retry: { maxRetries: 4, backoff: "exponential", jitter: true }

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@quickcommerce.com>, ops@quickcommerce.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, kevin@quickcommerce.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — QuickCommerce spike (Apr 28)

Elaine / Kevin / QC Ops —

Thanks again for working with us over the last 48 hours. Below is a short summary of what we found and the mitigation actions taken. Happy to hop on a follow-up call to walk through the postmortem and next steps.

What happened (summary):
- Timeline: 2027-04-28T15:44–15:52 PDT there was a short window where QC's observed p95/p99 and 502/504 rate spiked.
- Root cause: Retry amplification driven primarily by client-side SDK configuration (rwd-sdk-js@0.9.1) that used short timeouts and a faulty non-increasing backoff. When a small number of upstream slow responses appeared, the SDK retried aggressively (no jitter) and generated a large burst of duplicate requests. This amplified load created transient backend queueing and more 5xx responses, which in turn caused more client retries.

Actions taken:
- QuickCommerce agreed to update their SDK config to timeoutMs=30000 and exponential backoff with jitter (maxRetries=4). They reported pushing the change to a canary within the hour.
- Redwood enabled soft per-customer throttling for QC for 24 hours to prevent amplification (soft-429 path).
- We published an emergency patch to rwd-sdk-js (0.9.2) that fixes the backoff behavior; SDK docs and the snippet are attached.
- Follow-up: we opened SUP-1234 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234) to track a server-side mitigation that improves resiliency to short retry storms.

Impact: short-lived merchant checkout failures for ~8 minutes. No data leakage or policy violations detected.

Next steps and recommendations:
- We recommend QC roll the SDK patch (0.9.2) to production and keep the increased timeout/backoff settings.
- Redwood will add a targeted warning to the model endpoint when client retry rates exceed a threshold and will update our onboarding docs to flag safe default timeouts for SDKs.
- We'll schedule a follow-up call to review the full postmortem PDF (attached).

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_qc_20270430.pdf (postmortem), sdk-config-snippet.txt

If you'd like to schedule a 30-minute review tomorrow, I can coordinate.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
